q: Should a growing MSME set an absolute or an intensity emissions target?
title: Absolute or intensity emissions target?
short: Set an absolute target if a buyer, the SBTi or a programme asks for one; the SBTi SME route uses an absolute Scope 1 and 2 target. Track intensity alongside it, because a growing unit can cut emissions per tonne and still see total emissions rise. Many MSMEs publish both.
audience: MSMEs answering buyers and lenders on targets

sections.h: What each target tells a reader
ul: Absolute: total tonnes of CO2e in the target year against the base year. It is what the climate sees, and what science-based routes ask for.
Intensity: tonnes per unit of output, such as t CO2e per tonne of castings or per lakh pieces. It shows efficiency and is fair to a unit that is growing.
The GHG Protocol Corporate Standard, Chapter 11, describes both and notes that an intensity target can be met while absolute emissions rise.
SBTi SME route: an absolute Scope 1 and 2 reduction target under the Corporate Near-Term Criteria. The minimum cut depends on your base and target years; check it on the SBTi site.
India's CCTS: GHG emission intensity targets, per tonne of product, notified by sector for obligated entities.
Sustainability-linked loans: either, as written in the facility agreement; intensity is common for growing borrowers.
Buyers: often absolute for their own Scope 3, but many accept supplier intensity with production data.

ol: If someone sets the type for you, use it.
If you plan to grow output fast, set an intensity target for operations and report absolute emissions next to it every year.
If you can cut absolute emissions through solar, fuel switching or electrification while growing, set an absolute target; it is the stronger claim.

p: Use a physical unit that tracks the energy you use: tonnes, pieces or kWh delivered. Avoid revenue, which moves with prices and inflation. Keep the same unit and production definition every year.

example.title: Illustrative three years of growth
lines: Base year: 1,000 t CO2; output grows 15% a year; intensity falls 5% a year
Each year total emissions change by 1.15 x 0.95 = 1.0925, a 9.25% rise
After three years: 1,000 x 1.0925 x 1.0925 x 1.0925 = 1,304 t CO2
Intensity after three years: 0.95 x 0.95 x 0.95 = 0.857, about 14.3% lower
An intensity target is met; an absolute target is missed by a wide margin
example.note: Growth and efficiency rates are illustrative.

senseible: Senseible tracks absolute Scope 1 and 2 emissions from your monthly bills and invoices and shows intensity per unit of output, so both figures come from the same records.
